PLAN

EDI COMPANION GUIDE

(Refers to the Implementation Guides based on ASC X12 278 Version 005010X217)
Health Care Authorization Request for Review (278)

(Companion Guide v2)


Disclosure Statement:
This Companion Guide has been prepared for Plan partners who are ready to participate in 278 Request for Authorization Review transactions. It is in conjunction with the ASC X12 5010 version of HIPAA Technical Report Type 3.

If there are any changes to this document, it will be incorporated and published as a newer version at https://www..org/EDI

Preface:
Plan offers EDI 278 Request for Authorization Review as mandated by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) that supplements Technical Report Type 3 (TR3) of 5010.

This Companion Guide to the v5010 ASC X12N Implementation Guides clarifies and specifies the data content when exchanging electronically with Plan. Transmissions based on this companion guide, used in tandem with the v5010 ASC X12N Implementation Guides, are compliant with both ASC X12 syntax and those guides. This Companion Guide is intended to convey information that is within the framework of the ASC X12N Implementation Guides adopted for use under HIPAA. The Companion Guide is not intended to convey information that in any way exceeds the requirements or usages of data expressed in the Implementation Guides.

TABLE OF CONTENTS











INTRODUCTION

SCOPE

This Companion Guide has been prepared for Plan trading partners who are submitting the Request for Authorization review 278 ASC X12 electronically. It provides all necessary information regarding inquiry submission to . It can be used to clarify and get relevant information about transactions and operating rules.

OVERVIEW

The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) requires that all health insurance payers in United States comply with the EDI standards as established by the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS). This guide is meant to be used in conjunction with the Health Care Services Review request for Review (278) instructions established by the ASC X12 Standards for EDI.

This Companion Guide covers the following topics.
Connection and Exchange of Data
278 Request and Update Configuration Details
File Testing and Validation
Production 278 Requests and Updates
Reporting and Responses
Support

Please refer to the full ASC X12 005010X217 guide for the full collection of industry standard details for a 278 file.
http://www.x12.org

SUPPORT CONTACT INFORMATION
For all technical and support related questions concerning file trade, existing partners may contact the Plan EDI Team via email at edi@.org. 

TESTING WITH PLAN

Testing Process
The following process can be followed to perform testing with a Plan representative.

Ensure all appropriate agreements are in place before the exchange of data
Exchange all required details between  and your organization to configure SFTP connection.
Configure your 278 request file based on this Companion Guide and the X12 278 Standards.
Create and exchange the established 278 Authorization Testing Scenarios included in this guide below.
A Plan developer will review the exchanged 278 request files submitted and validate a successful data load. If there are any issues, the trading partner will be contacted and asked to correct the file and resubmit.
 related business teams will review the loaded Authorization for business validation.
The response files or reports are sent back to the originating partner for review and approval.
Once both parties approve production readiness, file trade in production will be implemented.

278 Testing Scenarios
To ensure a seamless implementation please provide authorization examples for the following test scenarios:
Inpatient And Outpatient Authorizations
Authorizations should include all related service codes and min/max unit ranges.
Initial vs Updated Authorizations for the following values:
Provider changes
Date of Service changes
Procedure changes
Status Change
Reconsideration Authorizations
Change in Units
Retro Auth Adjustments (Adjustments to auth with past Service Dates)
Voided Authorizations (If required)
Full Denied Authorizations
Partial Approved/Denial Units
Pending Authorizations

CONNECTIVITY/COMMUNICATIONS WITH PLAN

PROCESS FLOW
 performs 278 requests in batch. The sender does not remain connected while the receiver processes the transactions.

Process flow:

Trading Partner submits 278 requests to Plan via batch file.
 EDI Receives a 278 batch request.
SNIP Level 2 Validation Map Invoked
 EDI generates an optional response file (999)
Submitted 278 Authorization data is loaded to the  Authorization System for medical review.

RETRANSMISSION PROCEDURE
Retransmissions should be made on the following occasions:

Connectivity failure
A 999 acknowledgment is not received.
If partner needs to submit inquiry again

SYSTEM MAINTENANCE
In the case that Maintenance is required, the Plan Maintenance Window schedule begins on Saturdays at 6 PM and ends on Sundays by 10 PM. SFTP will be unavailable periodically during this time.





CONTROL SEGMENTS/ENVELOPES

General Notes
All data must be submitted in UPPER CASE.
Leading spaces must be omitted.
Trailing spaces must be omitted unless necessary to fulfill a minimum field length.

The 278 request files are expected to follow the above standard and values for the ISA-IEA, GS-GE, and ST-SE control segment values. All the other standard EDI segments that are specific to the transaction should be used as per X12 ASC 5010 Guide.

Control Segment Hierarchy
ISA - Interchange Control Header segment 
GS - Functional Group Header segment 
ST - Transaction Set Header segment 
First 278 Transaction 
SE - Transaction Set Trailer segment 
ST - Transaction Set Header segment 
Second 278 Transaction 
SE - Transaction Set Trailer segment 
ST - Transaction Set Header segment 
Third 278 Transaction 
SE - Transaction Set Trailer segment 
GE - Functional Group Trailer segment 
IEA - Interchange Control Trailer segment
 
Delimiters
It is recommended that the following delimiters be used when a 278 transaction is submitted.


 







PLAN SPECIFIC BUSINESS RULES AND LIMITATIONS

Authorization Rules
It is preferred that you send Provider NPI, Tax ID and City, State, Zip for Authorizations to process the transaction correctly.
You can submit a 2000F SV1 (Professional Service) and 2000F SV2 (Institutional Service), but they cannot be submitted on the same authorization file.  does not currently accept SV3 (Dental Service).
Once an Episode Type of IP or OP has been loaded to our Authorization system, it cannot be updated. The vendor will need to send a Cancelation and a new Authorization for the correct Episode Type.
Multiple Service Lines are accepted within each authorization.
Only ICD10 diagnosis codes will be accepted.
Decision date should be submitted in the Diagnosis Date Field Value [e.g. HI01-04]
Receive Date should be included in BHT04.
 will Populate Units based on Procedure Code Category and Service Dates
Approved Units need to be sent in HSD02.
Requested units will be sent in 2000F SV104. 

File Names
 will establish file naming conventions directly with the trading partners. 
E.g. <TRADINGPARTNER>_<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>__<SEQ#>_278_i_p


Placeholder ID’s

In certain cases, auth requests cannot proceed because valid provider information is unavailable at the time of submission. To meet the minimum requirement for a Requesting Provider ID, placeholder IDs must be used to avoid delays or errors in processing. This ensures that requests can be submitted even when data from  to Stanson is incomplete or missing.

UNKNOWN PRACTITIONER: 102301P00080803
UNKNOWN FACILITY: 102301S99999999-L001


















TRANSACTION SPECIFIC INFORMATION

 has created the following grid to assist in the design of the specific segments and values accepted by our organization. This table includes only those fields that  has a specific value set or provides additional guidance on the value sent. This table does not include all of the necessary fields to submit a successful transaction.

(Refers to the Implementation Guides based on ASC X12 820 Version ()


 

Disclosure Statement:
This Companion Guide has been prepared for Plan partners participating in sending the 820 Payroll Deducted and other Group Premium Transaction (X218). It is in conjunction with the ASC X12 820 Version  of HIPAA X12 Standards.

If there are any changes to this document, it will be incorporated and published as a newer version at https://www..org/EDI

Preface:
Plan accepts 820 Transactions as mandated by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) that supplements Technical Report Type 3 (TR3) of 5010.

This Companion Guide clarifies and specifies the data content when exchanging 820 X12 Transactions with Plan. Transmissions based on this companion guide, used in tandem with the ASC X12 820 Version  HIPAA Implementation Guides, are compliant with both ASC X12 syntax and those guides. This Companion Guide is intended to convey information that is within the framework of the ASC X12N Implementation Guides adopted for use under HIPAA. The Companion Guide is not intended to convey information that in any way exceeds the requirements or usages of data expressed in the Implementation Guides.

TABLE OF CONTENTS




















	
INTRODUCTION
SCOPE

This Companion Guide has been prepared for Plan Trading Partners who are submitting the 820 X12 (Version 218) Transactions to . It provides all necessary information regarding submission to  and will be used to clarify and receive relevant information about transactions and operating rules.

OVERVIEW

The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) requires that all Health Insurance Payers in the United States comply with the EDI standards as established by the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS). This companion guide is meant to be used in conjunction with the 820 Implementation Guide Version  established by the ASC X12 Standards for EDI.  This transaction set is not intended to replace the Health Care Claim Payment/Advice Transaction Set (835) and therefore, will not be used for account payment posting.

This Companion Guide covers the following topics:
Connection and Exchange of Data
820 Configuration Details
File Testing and Validation
Production 820 Transaction Details
Reporting
Support

Please refer to the full ASC X12  Implementation Guide for the expanded information of industry standard details.
http://www.x12.org

SUPPORT CONTACT INFORMATION
For all technical and support related questions concerning file trade, existing partners may contact the Plan EDI Team via email at edi@.org. 

TESTING WITH PLAN

Testing Process
The following process can be followed to perform testing with a Plan representative.

Ensure all appropriate agreements are in place before the exchange of data.
Exchange all required details between  and your organization to configure SFTP connection.
Configure your 820 X12 file based on this Companion Guide and the X12 820 Implementation Standards.
Create and exchange the 820 Testing scenarios.
Plan Business Teams will review the Test 820 files to validate acceptance.  If the file is rejected, the Trading Partner will be contacted to correct the file and resubmit.
Once both parties agree to Production readiness, the Trading Partner will be approved to submit Production files.




CONNECTIVITY/COMMUNICATIONS WITH PLAN
PROCESS FLOW

Trading Partner submits an 820 file to Plan.
Submitted 820 data is validated via SNIP Level 2 and data is then loaded into the appropriate tables. 
If any errors are found, the entire file will be rejected and needs to be resubmitted.
Validated data is loaded into appropriate tables.

RETRANSMISSION PROCEDURE
Retransmissions will need to be made when the following occurs:
Connectivity failure
820 file is rejected 

SYSTEM MAINTENANCE
In the case maintenance is required, Plan will notify Trading Partners via email of scheduled system downtime.

CONTROL SEGMENTS/ENVELOPES

General Notes
Leading spaces must be omitted.
Trailing spaces must be omitted unless necessary to fulfill a minimum field length.  




The 820 files are expected to follow the standard values for the ISA-IEA, GS-GE, BHT, and ST-SE control segment values. All other standard EDI segments specific to the transaction should be used as per X12 ASC 820 Implementation Guide.

 Disclosure Statement:
This Companion Guide contains the requirements for  Plan Trading Partners in exchanging the 837I (Institutional) X12 Claims File transactions. This document is to be used in conjunction with the ASC X12 837I Version 005010X223A1 of the approved HIPAA WPC Implementation Guides.

Any changes to this document, if needed, will be updated and published as a newer version at https://www..org/EDI.

Preface:
This transaction set is used by Trading Partners to submit Institutional (UB40/Hospital) Healthcare Claim Billing information, Encounter information, or both, from Providers of Healthcare services either directly or via intermediary billers or clearinghouses.  If requested by the Trading Partners, will return a 999 acknowledgement to verify acceptance and/or rejections within the 837I.   These transactions are mandated by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) that supplements Technical Report Type 3 (TR3) of 5010.

This Companion Document, along with the 005010X223A1 Implementation Guide, specifies the data content when exchanging electronically with  Plan. Transmissions based on these documents are compliant with the Version 5010 ASC X12 syntax requirements and are intended to convey information that is within the framework of the ASC X12N Implementation Guides for use under HIPAA. The Companion Guide is not intended to convey information that in any way exceeds the requirements or usages of data expressed in the Implementation Guides.

TABLE OF CONTENTS
INTRODUCTION
SCOPE

This Companion Guide is for  Plan Trading Partners who are submitting the 837I Institutional (Hospital/UB40) Healthcare Claim Billing information, Encounter information, or both, from Providers of Healthcare services. It provides all necessary information regarding 837I submissions to . It can be used to clarify and get relevant information about transactions and operating rules.

OVERVIEW

The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) requires that all health insurance payers in the United States comply with the EDI standards as established by the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS). 

This Companion Guide covers the following topics:
Connection and Exchange of 837I File Submissions.
Configuration Details

Reporting and Responses
Support

http://www.x12.org

SUPPORT CONTACT INFORMATION
For all technical and support related questions concerning file trade, existing partners may contact the  Plan EDI Team via email at edi@.org. 

TESTING WITH CARE SERVICES

Testing Process
The following process can be followed to perform testing with a care Services representative.

Ensure all appropriate agreements are in place before the exchange of data.
Exchange all required details between  and your organization to configure SFTP connection.
Configure your 837I Claims file based on this Companion Guide and the 837I Implementation Guide Standards.
Create and exchange 837I Testing Scenarios.  
A  Plan representative will review the exchanged 837I Test Files submitted and validate a successful data load. 
If a file is not accepted or rejects during testing, the trading partner will be contacted and asked to correct the file and resubmit.
 related business teams will review the loaded 837I Claims Files.
Once and the submitting Trading Partner approve validation of test files, the Trading Partner will be activated to submit production files to .



837I Testing Scenarios

To ensure a seamless implementation, please provide examples for the following test scenarios:
Files containing various claim examples- Medicare, Medicaid, Commercial etc.
Claims containing Subscriber/Dependent insurance examples.
Files containing procedures for Institutional services such as- In Patient Hospital/Skilled Nursing Facility/Rural Health etc.
COB claims/Primary-Secondary coverage.
Claims containing one service line (2400 Loop) and claims with multiple service lines.
Several resubmission claims (CLM05= 7).
Claims to a Trading Partner that should reject at back to the Trading Partner.
Claims containing incorrect information that should cause a claim to reject on the front end.


CONNECTIVITY/COMMUNICATIONS WITH  PLAN SERVICES
PROCESS FLOW
Trading Partner submits 837I X12 file to  Plan.
 EDI generates a 999 acknowledgement (if requested by the Trading Partner) after processing the file to ensure it is syntactically correct- Accepted or Rejected- and returns the 999 to Submitting Trading Partner.
277ca will be submitted to Trading Partner after claims are processed into adjudication system.

RETRANSMISSION PROCEDURE
Retransmissions will be required when there are:

Connectivity failures.
Rejected segments within a 999 or rejected claims noted on the 277ca.

SYSTEM MAINTENANCE	

In the case maintenance is required,  Plan will notify Trading Partners via email of scheduled system downtime.

	
CONTROL SEGMENTS/ENVELOPES

General Notes
Leading spaces must be omitted.
Trailing spaces must be omitted unless necessary to fulfill a minimum field length.
During Testing- ISA015 must be “T” for Test.


The 837I X12 Claims file is expected to follow the standard values for the ISA-IEA, GS-GE, and ST-SE control segment values. All other standard EDI segments specific to the transaction should be used as per X12 ASC 5010 Guide.

PLAN

EDI COMPANION GUIDE

Refers to the Implementation Guides based on ASC X12 5010A Version ()
X12 Health Care Claims Professional (837P)


 

Disclosure Statement:
This Companion Guide contains the requirements for  Plan Trading Partners in exchanging the 837P (Professional) X12 Claims File transactions. This document is to be used in conjunction with the ASC X12 837P Version  of the approved HIPAA X12 Implementation Guides.

Any changes to this document, if needed, will be updated and published as a newer version at https://www..org/EDI.

Preface:
This transaction set is used by Trading Partners to submit Professional (Medical) Healthcare Claim Billing information, Encounter information, or both, from Providers of Healthcare services either directly or via intermediary billers or clearinghouses.   will return a 999 acknowledgement (if requested by Submitter) to the Trading Partners to verify acceptance and/or rejections within the 837P.   These transactions are mandated by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) that supplements Technical Report Type 3 (TR3) of 5010.

This Companion Document, along with the  Implementation Guide, clarifies and specifies the data content when exchanging electronically with  Plan. Transmissions based on these documents are compliant with the Version 5010A1 ASC X12 syntax requirements and are intended to convey information that is within the framework of the ASC X12N Implementation Guides for use under HIPAA. The Companion Guide is not intended to convey information that in any way exceeds the requirements or usages of data expressed in the Implementation Guides.

TABLE OF CONTENTS
INTRODUCTION
SCOPE

This Companion Guide is for  Plan Trading Partners who are submitting the 837 Professional (Medical) Healthcare Claim Billing information, Encounter information, or both, from Providers of Healthcare services. It provides all necessary information regarding 837P submission to . It can be used to clarify and get relevant information about transactions and operating rules.

OVERVIEW

The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) requires that all health insurance payers in the United States comply with the EDI standards as established by the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS). 

This Companion Guide covers the following topics:
Connection and Exchange of 837P File Submissions.
Configuration Details
File Testing and Validation
Reporting and Responses
Support

Please refer to the full ASC X12  guide for the full collection of industry standard details for an 837P X12 file.
http://www.x12.org

SUPPORT CONTACT INFORMATION
For all technical and support related questions concerning file trade, existing partners may contact the  Plan  EDI Team via email at edi@.org. 

TESTING WITH  PLAN

Testing Process
The following should be followed to perform testing with a  Plan EDI representative.

Ensure all appropriate agreements are in place before the exchange of data.
Exchange all required details between  and your organization to configure SFTP connection.
Configure your 837P Claims file based on this Companion Guide and the 837P Implementation Guide Standards.
Create and exchange 837P Testing Scenarios.  
A  Plan representative will review the exchanged 837P Test Files submitted and validate a successful data load. 
If a file rejects during testing, the trading partner will be contacted and asked to correct the file and resubmit.
999 Acknowledgments, either Accepted or Rejected, will be returned if requested by submitting Trading Partner.
Once both  and Trading Partner approve validation of test files, the Trading Partner will be activated to submit production files to .




837P Testing Scenarios

To ensure a seamless implementation, please provide examples for the following test scenarios:
Files containing various claim examples- Medicare, Medicaid, Commercial etc.
Claims containing Subscriber/Dependent insurance examples.
Files containing procedures for Professional services such as- Office/Hospital/Nursing Home/Ambulance etc.
COB claims/Primary-Secondary coverage.
Claims containing one service line (2400 Loop) and claims with several service lines.
Several resubmission claims (CLM05= 7).
Claims to a Trading Partner that should reject at  back to the Trading Partner.
Claims containing incorrect information that should cause a claim to reject on the front end.

CONNECTIVITY/COMMUNICATIONS WITH CARE SERVICES
        PROCESS FLOW

Trading Partner submits 837P X12 file to  Plan.
 EDI generates a 999 acknowledgement (if requested by the Trading Partner) after processing the file to ensure it is syntactically correct- Accepted or Rejected- and return the 999 to Submitting Trading Partner.
277ca will be submitted to Trading Partner after claims are processed into adjudication system.


RETRANSMISSION PROCEDURE
Retransmissions will be required when there are:

Connectivity failures.
Rejected segments within a 999 or rejected claims noted on the 277ca.

       SYSTEM MAINTENANCE
In the case maintenance is required,  Plan will notify Trading Partners via email of scheduled system downtimes.

CONTROL SEGMENTS/ENVELOPES

General Notes
Leading spaces must be omitted.
Trailing spaces must be omitted unless necessary to fulfill a minimum field length.
During Testing- ISA015 must be “T” for Test.



The 837P X12 Claims file is expected to follow the standard values for the ISA-IEA, GS-GE, and ST-SE control segment values. All other standard EDI segments specific to the transaction should be used as per X12 ASC 5010 Guide.




Control Segment Hierarchy

ISA - Interchange Control Header segment 
GS - Functional Group Header segment 
ST - Transaction Set Header segment 
First 837 Transaction 
SE - Transaction Set Trailer segment 
ST - Transaction Set Header segment 
Second 837 Transaction 
SE - Transaction Set Trailer segment 
ST - Transaction Set Header segment 
Third 837 Transaction 
SE - Transaction Set Trailer segment 
GE - Functional Group Trailer segment 
IEA - Interchange Control Trailer segment
 


Delimiters

 


CARE SERVICES SPECIFIC BUSINESS RULES AND LIMITATIONS
       
File Names:
 will establish file naming conventions directly with the trading partners. 
E.g. <TRADINGPARTNER>_<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>__<SEQ#>_837P










TRANSACTION SPECIFIC INFORMATION

SERVICES

EDI COMPANION GUIDE 

(Refers to the Implementation Guides based on ASC X12 N 834 Version )

Health Care Benefit Enrollment and Maintenance (834)

(Companion Guide v1)

Disclosure Statement:
This Companion Guide has been prepared for  Services partners who are ready to participate in 834 Request for Authorization Review and Response transactions. It is in conjunction with the ASC X12 5010 version of HIPAA Technical Report Type 3.

If there are any changes to this document, it will be incorporated and published as a newer version at https://www..org/EDI

Preface:
 Services offers EDI 834 Benefit Enrollment and Maintenance as mandated by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) that supplements Technical Report Type 3 (TR3) of 5010.

This Companion Guide to the v5010 ASC X12N Implementation Guides clarifies and specifies the data content when exchanging electronically with  Services. Transmissions based on this companion guide, used in tandem with the v5010 ASC X12N Implementation Guides, are compliant with both ASC X12 syntax and those guides. This Companion Guide is intended to convey information that is within the framework of the ASC X12N Implementation Guides adopted for use under HIPAA. The Companion Guide is not intended to convey information that in any way exceeds the requirements or usages of data expressed in the Implementation Guides.

INTRODUCTION

SCOPE

This companion guide has been prepared for  Services trading partners who are submitting the healthcare benefit enrollment and maintenance 834 ASC X12 electronically. It provides all necessary information regarding inquiry submission to . It can be used to clarify and get relevant information about transactions and operating rules.

OVERVIEW

The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPPA) from 1996 contains provisions for administrative simplification.  This required the HHS (Department of Health and Human Services) to create and adopt standards for EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) for transactions between covered entities. The ANSI standard spells out the segments and valid values for fields that are to be used for a EDI transaction to be compliant.

This Companion Guide covers the following topics.
Connection and Exchange of Data
834 Benefit Enrollment and Maintenance Configuration Details
File Testing and Validation
Support

Please refer to the full ASC X12 004010X095 guide for the full collection of industry standard details for an 834 file.
http://www.x12.org

SUPPORT CONTACT INFORMATION
For all technical and support related questions concerning file trade, existing partners may contact the  Services EDI Team via email at edi@.org. 

TESTING WITH  SERVICES

Testing Process
The following process can be followed to perform testing with a  Services representative.

Ensure all appropriate agreements are in place before the exchange of data
Exchange all required details between  and your organization to configure SFTP connection.
Configure your 834 Benefit Enrollment and Maintenance file based on this Companion Guide and the X12 834 Standards.
Create and exchange the established 834 Testing Scenarios included in this guide below.
A  Services developer will review the exchanged 834 files submitted and validate a successful data load. If there are any issues, the trading partner will be contacted and asked to correct the file and resubmit.
 related business teams will review the loaded 834 file for business validation.
Once both parties approve production readiness, file trade in production will be implemented.



834 Testing Scenarios
To ensure a seamless implementation please provide Benefit Enrollment and Maintenance examples for the following test scenarios:
Create a new sale with a family of 4 enrollment, as this is the most common scenario for families.
Set up a family of 6 enrollment to validate the family rating rule when there are 3 dependents under age 21.
Complete a single enrollment, which is the most common scenario for individuals.
Add a child to an existing enrollment, which frequently occurs as a child-only addition.
Cancel a spouse from a policy, a routine day-to-day scenario.
Remove a child from a policy, another frequent scenario encountered daily.
Cancel an entire family’s enrollment, reflecting common day-to-day operations.
Terminate a child from the policy, which is a typical occurrence.
Terminate the entire family from the policy, a scenario often faced in daily processing.
Add a dependent during Open Enrollment to capture changes affecting eligibility or rating.
Make basic enrollment maintenance updates, such as changes to email or phone information.
Update demographic information by processing a common address change request.
Process a change in demographic information by updating the date of birth (DOB).
Handle scenarios where same family attempts to enroll more than once, ensuring proper cancellation or termination based on policy status.
Attempt to enroll a family member with an unsupported relationship code to confirm the issuer’s error handling.
Reinstate a subscriber to restore an entire contract.
Reinstate a subscriber to reactivate a dependent under an existing contract.

CONNECTIVITY/COMMUNICATIONS WITH  SERVICES

PROCESS FLOW

Trading Partner submits 834 to  Services via SFTP.
 EDI Receives the 834 file and will be processed sequentially in the order received.
SNIP Level 2 Validation Map Invoked
 EDI generates an optional response file (999)

RETRANSMISSION PROCEDURE
Retransmissions should be made on the following occasions:

Connectivity failure
A 999 response is not received.
If partner needs to submit inquiry again

SYSTEM MAINTENANCE
In the case that Maintenance is required, the  Services Maintenance Window schedule begins on Saturdays at 6 PM and ends on Sundays by 10 PM. SFTP will be unavailable periodically during this time.





CONTROL SEGMENTS/ENVELOPES

General Notes
All data must be submitted in UPPER CASE.
Leading spaces must be omitted.
Trailing spaces must be omitted unless necessary to fulfill a minimum field length.

The 834 files are expected to follow the above standard and values for the ISA-IEA, GS-GE, and ST-SE control segment values. All the other standard EDI segments that are specific to the transaction should be used as per X12 ASC 5010 Guide.

Control Segment Hierarchy
ISA - Interchange Control Header segment 
GS - Functional Group Header segment 
ST - Transaction Set Header segment 
First 834 Transaction 
SE - Transaction Set Trailer segment 
ST - Transaction Set Header segment 
Second 834 Transaction 
SE - Transaction Set Trailer segment 
ST - Transaction Set Header segment 
Third 834 Transaction 
SE - Transaction Set Trailer segment 
GE - Functional Group Trailer segment 
IEA - Interchange Control Trailer segment
 
Delimiters
It is recommended that the following delimiters be used when an 834 transaction is submitted.


 
 SERVICES SPECIFIC BUSINESS RULES AND LIMITATIONS
File Names
 will establish file naming conventions directly with the trading partners. 
Example: <TRADINGPARTNER>__<YYYYMMDD>.834.i.g

TRANSACTION SPECIFIC INFORMATION

 has created the following grid to assist in the design of the specific segments and values accepted by our organization. This table includes only those fields that  has a specific value set or provides additional guidance on the value sent. This table does not include all of the necessary fields to submit a successful transaction. 












APPENDICES


Transmission Examples

Scenario 1: Enroll an Employee in Multiple Health Care Insurance Products

John Doe is enrolling in three health care products -- health, dental, and vision. He also has Coordination of Benefits (COB) with another insurance company.












Scenario 2 -- Add a Dependent (Full-time Student) to an Existing Enrollment

James E. Doe, the son of John Doe, is being enrolled under John Doe's medical coverage. James is enrolled at Penn State and expects to graduate on 5/15/1998. His Social Security Number is 103229876. The enrollment for the subscriber, John Doe, had to be submitted before his dependents can be enrolled.

This X12 Transaction Set contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Health Care
Information Status Notification Transaction Set �277� for use within the context of an Electronic Data
Interchange �EDI� environment. This transaction set can be used by a health care payer or authorized
agent to notify a provider, recipient, or authorized agent regarding the status of a health care claim or
encounter or to request additional information from the provider regarding a health care claim or
encounter, health care services review, or transactions related to the provisions of health care. This
transaction set is not intended to replace the Health Care Claim Payment/Advice Transaction Set �835�
and therefore, will not be used for account payment posting. The notification may be at a summary or
service line detail level. The notification may be solicited or unsolicited.
